title: Water Tank Conservation Decision — Central Plant

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitcomb
transcript.text: Dana Whitcomb. The Central Plant tank is at 39,100 gallons and falling at about 2,200 gallons an hour, which gives us about 18 hours. The tank is refilled from the city main by a float valve, so it will start taking advisory water as soon as the level drops. I can close the city fill valve now and protect what we have, or let it top up and hope the advisory is nothing. The cooling tower make-up alone uses about 600 gallons an hour. I need a decision.

transcript.speaker: Helen Marchetti
transcript.text: Understood. Close the city fill valve now. Initiate conservation protocol in order of clinical impact: reduce cooling tower make-up by running chillers on lower load, pause laundry and non-clinical uses, turn off irrigation. We need to preserve stored water for essential clinical use.

instructorNote: This inject tests the AOC’s authority to override operational discretion and order a conservation protocol. Watch for whether the AOC explicitly authorizes the action and confirms the conservation order.
